newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey rejects Euro parliament media freedom call.
newsitem.headline: Turkey rejects Euro parliament media freedom call.

text.p: Turkey on Tuesday rejected a call from the European Parliament for Ankara to refrain from restricting media freedom as a move that was premature and damaging to the parliament's image among Turkish people.

"There is no common sense explanation...for the European Parliament's new decision against Turkey, when no text has been presented to the Turkish Parliament or even officially discussed by the government," a foreign ministry spokesman said.
Spokesman Omer Akbel said in a statement the resolution was based on rumours in the Turkish press and was a fresh example of the European Parliament's prejudice towards Turkey.
On December 12, the EU parliament adopted a resolution calling on the Turkish government "to abandon its plans to restrict the freedom of the press".

The resolution also charged that journalists had been imprisoned, abducted and assassinated in Turkey. Under existing laws Turkish journalists and writers can be jailed for articles deemed to support Kurdish separatism.

"It is unimaginable that steps against contemporary norms would be taken to limit the freedom of the press or conscience at a time when Turkey has begun a reform initiative in the field of human rights," Akbel said.
The justice minister said in November the government would impose fines on media organs which insulted the state.

The Turkish media has given high profile in recent weeks to a scandal linking the state with underworld gangs which erupted after a top police official died in an accident in the same car as a government deputy and a gangster.
For months beforehand, Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan had been warning the secularist press that he would act against what he saw as biased and unfair reporting.
The European Parliament, already angered by Turkey's shaky human rights record, voted in October to block hundreds of millions of dollars in aid to help Ankara set up a customs union with the EU.
